_note: Per-post thematic summaries from TAO analysis. Each entry is a list of theme statements — concise, opinionated one-liners about what the post argues. These also live in each post's frontmatter as 'themes:'.
nora-bateson-how-our-ways-of-knowing-sha: Applying static, context-free data to living systems is dangerous
Warm data contextualises information through relationships, as an alternative to reductionism
Systems thinking as an ethical stance, inherited from Gregory Bateson
is-conversation-still-a-useful-metaphor: Conversation metaphor as increasingly inadequate for GenAI
Anthropomorphism as a structural side effect of conversation design
Alternative interaction metaphors: delegation, thinking, note-taking
Metacognition and inner dialog as possible paradigms for human-AI interaction
why-chatgpt-is-bullshit-and-why-we-shoul: LLMs as structurally indifferent to truth, not accidentally wrong
Grice's cooperative principle as the violated contract
Cognitive laziness as the human vulnerability that makes this dangerous
Design as the response: keeping humans caring about truth
conversational-interfaces-are-not-easy: Conversational interfaces are poorly suited to non-linear tasks like writing
Two new AI user behaviors: accordion editing and apple picking
The articulation barrier as a specific usability threshold
Direct manipulation as the design response
context-engineering-lets-call-it-design: Context engineering is a rebranding of work designers and authors have always done
Semantic information types as the structural logic behind good context windows
Design vocabulary maps directly onto prompt engineering: information architecture, instructional design, technical authoring
Inviting designers and authors to the GenAI table as a practical recommendation
llm-hallucinations-knowledge-as-missing-: LLM hallucinations are structurally unsolvable without changing the underlying mechanism
Confabulation as a more precise term: filling gaps with plausible fabrications, not random errors
The missing fundamental as an analogy: truth can only be approximated in LLMs, never caught
The impossibility of a genuine TRUE/FALSE binary state in probabilistic systems
thinking-in-action-precision-matters: Precise terminology as a prerequisite for clear thinking
Dialectical thinking as the antidote to epistemic bias
The distinction between opinion, conviction, argument, and rhetoric
LLMs reinforce rather than correct our tendency to avoid dialectical challenge
a-digital-garden-as-central-space: The early web enabled a kind of personal expression that the algorithm era has taken away
Non-linear thinking needs a non-linear writing environment — not a blog, not a social feed
A digital garden is the right infrastructure for how my mind actually works
Serendipity is an organising principle, not a side effect
Writing as craft requires a space that doesn't talk back and doesn't distract
AI has a legitimate role in the garden, but only as assistant — never as author
chatgpt-presentation-prep: The value of AI as a feedback loop lies not in the quality of its output but in the quality of articulation it provokes from the user.
Procrastination and presentation anxiety are often articulation problems, not motivation problems — and that reframes what a useful tool looks like.
Voice-mode AI works because it removes the pressure of judgment while preserving the benefit of an audience, a combination humans rarely offer.
Iterative spoken rehearsal with transcription is a legitimate structured methodology, even when the AI's analytical feedback is mediocre.
Fitting a tool to a cognitive style is more powerful than forcing a cognitive style to fit a tool.
7-new-skills-for-conversation-designers-: The content/code boundary is a false constraint: conversation designers who learn NLU and Python become fundamentally more capable, not just more versatile.
Entities, not intents, are the underexploited building block of robust conversational systems — a systematic entity model is the conversation designer's equivalent of an information architecture.
Knowledge graphs represent the logical ceiling of entity thinking: they transform a conversational interface from a command-and-response tool into a navigable semantic universe.
Conversational AI sits uncomfortably between IT and content, and that organisational ambiguity is itself a design problem that practitioners must learn to solve.
Skill expansion for conversation designers in 2022 is not about chasing trends but about closing the gap between what language professionals know and what the technology now demands.
instagram: Claude Code's plugin ecosystem frames AI capabilities as professional team roles
Plugins as delegation: assigning developer responsibilities to specialized agentic tools
china-s-approach-to-ai-anthropomorphism: China's AI law frames human cognitive vulnerability to anthropomorphism as a harm worth regulating
AI regulation as a design context: law sets requirements that shape technical choices
Anthropomorphism as a legal category, not just a design risk
air-canadas-bot-mishap-pre-dates-chatgpt: The Air Canada chatbot story is routinely misread as an LLM failure, when it was actually a mundane content governance failure that predates generative AI entirely.
Content siloes are the real enemy of reliable conversational AI — not model capability or hallucination.
Single sourcing — write once, configure for many — is the structural solution to cross-channel content inconsistency, whether your bot is NLU-based or LLM-based.
Content should be treated as structured, granular, metadated data rather than freeform prose, to enable omnichannel consistency.
The tooling problem in conversational AI is not just about the model; it's about dashboards that expose content component relationships, channel dependencies, and release provenance.
saturday-design-thoughts: Silence is not an absence of design but a design material in its own right — and LLMs, left unchecked, destroy it.
The 'gift of the gab' of current LLM interfaces is a conscious big-tech design decision, not a technical inevitability, which means it can be undone.
Meaningful friction — designing constraint and hesitation into an LLM — is a more honest interaction model than frictionless completion.
Music and singing reveal that silence shapes and co-creates meaning; the same principle applies to conversational AI, where the unspoken is as significant as the spoken.
System prompting is a legitimate philosophical and design lever for building receptive, silence-informed LLM behaviour.
hey-chatgpt-whos-the-boss: ChatGPT's apparent knowledge of post-cutoff events is best explained by probabilistic co-occurrence, not by internet access or deliberate training
Understanding LLMs as probabilistic models demystifies seemingly surprising outputs
Million-to-one probabilistic coincidences are an underexplored explanation for AI behavior
what-happens-when-ai-has-read-everything: The quality of LLM training data is not just a technical constraint but a humanistic one: books are valuable precisely because they are the product of sustained human effort and judgment.
Synthetic training data generated without human readership is not a solution but a category error—it mistakes the statistical form of knowledge for its substance.
Proposals to harvest human speech through surveillance ('dongles around our necks') reveal a troubling instrumentalisation of human communication as raw material.
A training loop in which AI feeds its own outputs back into itself as training data risks an epistemically closed system, detached from human experience and novelty.
The looming data scarcity crisis exposes a deeper question: if AI cannot originate, can it ever produce genuine literary novelty, style, or genre?
new-paper-from-microsoft-this-is-an-impo: Limits of LLM delegation in knowledge work
Failure modes of agentic AI on long-horizon tasks
Benchmarking what looks like capability versus what actually holds up
visualising-birdsong-as-data: Sound as structured information, not just aesthetic
Visualising the invisible to make patterns legible
Nature as encoded signal versus art as creativity
robin-interactions-shared-manifolds: Process and tooling behind acoustic visualisation
dont-show-me-your-ai: AI critique as a moral and political project, not just technical
Synthetic intimacy as the barrier to critical engagement
Mapping the political economy of AI: labor, infrastructure, data, environment, power
fieldwork-for-future-ecologies-onomatope: Art-based research is a legitimate and necessary form of environmental and climate knowledge-making, not merely supplementary to scientific fieldwork.
The 'field' is not a neutral site but a politically and ecologically charged location that must be reimagined through speculative and creative practice.
Non-human worlds and multispecies entanglements demand methodologies that go beyond anthropocentric sensing, including sound, movement, and image.
Radical ecological futures require radical artistic practices — speculation and proposition are political acts.
ai-artificialintelligence-behavior-behav: AI is not merely a tool but an active third cognitive system that restructures how humans reason and decide.
Uncritical deference to AI — 'cognitive surrender' — creates asymmetric risk: gains when AI is right, sharp losses when it is wrong.
The dual-process model of cognition is no longer sufficient; behavioral science must reckon with hybrid human-AI cognition.
The shift to System 3 raises governance questions about accountability, autonomy, and who controls the external layer of cognition.
the-ai-draft-a-process-essay-nobody-aske: AI-assisted writing is best understood as an editorial collaboration, not a ghostwriting shortcut
The cultural stigma around AI writing tools is driven more by ego and fear than by genuine ethical concern
The hardest part of writing has never been drafting, it has always been editing and shaping meaning
Productive resistance from an imperfect collaborator is the mechanism by which a writer discovers what they actually think
announcing-supercharged-human: Critical AI literacy must be actively designed and taught, not assumed to emerge naturally from exposure to technology.
Digital technologies are not neutral: they embed power structures, environmental costs, and epistemic risks that require deliberate civic response.
Young people need co-created, playful, and critical resources to become agents of the digital world rather than its passive subjects.
Combating the overlap between the information crisis and the climate crisis requires cross-sector collaboration between civil society, media, and educators.
prompt-thought-summaries: The traditional notion that summarisation requires a source text is a human-centric assumption that breaks down when working with LLMs.
LLMs are structurally better at constructing text from concepts than at reducing full texts — making keyword-first prompting a more effective summary strategy.
Human summarisation is cognitively sophisticated, drawing on deep semantic and rhetorical understanding; LLMs substitute this with superficial container-filling heuristics.
The best prompt Maaike found essentially asked the model to discard the source text entirely — revealing that the text itself may be unnecessary scaffolding when prompting for summaries.
Counterintuitive prompting strategies (construction over reduction) expose hidden assumptions in how we map human writing processes onto LLM capabilities.
